entities.summary: The Prečista Krajinska is the name for the ruins of a church located in the region of Skadarska Krajina, southeastern Montenegro. It was the second burial site of Jovan Vladimir, the ruler of Duklja, after his widow Kosara renewed it and transferred his remains from Prespa. The relics drew many devotees to the church, which became a center of pilgrimage. Kosara was interred in the church, at the feet of her husband, on her request. In around 1215—when Krajina was under the rule of Serbian Grand Prince Stefan Nemanjić—the relics were presumably removed from this church and transported to Dyrrhachium by the troops of Michael I, the despot of Epirus.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Prečista Krajinska played a significant role in the religious and cultural landscape of medieval Southern Europe, particularly in the region of Skadarska Krajina. Its relics drew many devotees to the church, which became a center of pilgrimage.
